description: The chart illustrates the number of hateful communication datasets published each year, broken down by researcher location categories shown in the legend. The horizontal axis lists the categories as years from 2012 through 2022 in chronological order and is labeled “Year.” The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^0\), \(10^1\), and \(10^2\) (covering roughly 1 to just over 100). For each year, multiple narrow, side-by-side bars represent locations: Other (blue), USA (orange), IN (green), UK (red), IT (purple), and DE (brown), with no stacking. Early years show only a few bars near the \(10^0\) level (e.g., USA around 2 in 2012 and 2013, USA around 1 in 2014, Other around 2 in 2014 and around 3 in 2015, and DE around 1 in 2015). From 2016 onward, grouped bars appear more consistently, with values spanning from about 1 up to above \(10^2\); for example, in 2017 Other is around the high teens, USA around the mid-teens, UK around 9, IT around 5, IN around 1, and DE is not visibly prominent, while in 2018 Other is around 30, USA around 12, and IN/UK/IT/DE are each around 4. In 2019 the bars include Other around 50, USA around 16, IN around 6, IT around 8, UK around 4, and DE around 2; in 2020 Other is near 90, USA around 40, IN around 12, UK around 15, IT around 2, and DE around 18. In 2021 Other reaches the tallest bar at a bit above \(10^2\) (just over 100), with USA around the mid-40s, IN around 20, UK around 17, IT around 12, and DE around 9. In 2022 the visible bars are lower and include Other around the mid-20s, IN around 9, UK around 8, USA around 3, IT around 1, and DE not clearly visible; no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the color coding, and the bars are not sorted by height within each year.
